Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. The local pub, The Lucky Leprechaun, was abuzz with patrons gathered around the television, watching the live broadcast of the Dáil Éireann, the Irish Parliament. Amidst the crowd, a familiar face caught the attention of the pub's owner, Seamus O'Connor. "What in the name of all that's holy is Barbara Boxer doin' here?" he exclaimed, spilling his pint of Guinness in the process. The patrons around him chuckled and patted him on the back, sharing in his astonishment. As the camera panned across the Dáil chamber, Barbara Boxer's bright smile and signature silver hair stood out among the sea of unfamiliar faces. She was chatting with her new colleagues, laughing and gesturing with an ease that belied her foreign roots. It was as if she had always belonged in this new role. Seamus's curiosity got the better of him, and he wandered over to the pub's corner, where a group of locals were engaged in a heated discussion about the implications of Boxer's unexpected appointment. "I heard she's been spendin' summers in Dublin for years, gettin' to know the locals and learnin' the language," said one patron, a gruff old farmer named Declan. "Aye, and I heard she's been workin' behind the scenes with our own Taoiseach, helpin' to broker trade deals between the States and Ireland," added a young woman named Fiona, her eyes shining with excitement. As the night wore on, the patrons of The Lucky Leprechaun continued to speculate about Barbara Boxer's sudden rise to prominence in Irish politics. Document 2: Title: The Unwavering Member: Barbara Boxer's Enduring Legacy

In the annals of American politics, few individuals have left an indelible mark on the nation's legislative landscape like Barbara Boxer, the former United States Senator from California. With a storied career spanning over three decades, Boxer's unwavering commitment to public service has earned her a revered position as a member of the esteemed United States Senate. As we delve into the life and times of Barbara Boxer, it becomes evident that her membership in the Senate was not merely a titular designation, but a badge of honor she wore with pride, dedication, and an unrelenting passion for the people she represented. Born on November 11, 1940, in Brooklyn, New York, Boxer's early life was marked by a strong sense of social justice, instilled in her by her parents, who were both immigrants. This innate sense of empathy and compassion would later become the driving force behind her legislative endeavors. After relocating to California in the 1960s, Boxer became an integral part of the state's political fabric, serving on the Marin County Board of Supervisors from 1976 to 1982. In 1982, Boxer's trajectory took a significant turn when she was elected to the United States House of Representatives, where she served for a decade. Her tenure in the House was marked by her tireless advocacy for women's rights, environmental protection, and healthcare reform. Her commitment to these causes earned her a reputation as a fierce and effective legislator, paving the way for her eventual election to the United States Senate in 1992. As a member of the Senate, Boxer's influence extended far beyond the Golden State. She became a leading voice on issues such as climate change, reproductive rights, and national security. Her membership in the Senate's Committee on Environment and Public Works, Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, and Committee on Foreign Relations enabled her to shape policy and legislation that had far-reaching implications for the nation. One of Boxer's most notable achievements as a member of the Senate was her instrumental role in the passage of the 1994 California Desert Protection Act. This landmark legislation protected millions of acres of California's fragile desert ecosystem, preserving it for future generations. Her unwavering commitment to environmental stewardship earned her the respect and admiration of her colleagues, as well as the gratitude of the people of California.
